messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for a great call earlier today — wanted to capture the key outcomes and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of ask / constraints
- Primary asks:
  - Target SLOs for interactive experiences (short prompts, <=512 tokens) across regions.
  - Sustained concurrency/throughput baseline and expected burst patterns.
  - Streaming token latency targets for token-by-token UI updates.
  - Regional routing / data residency constraints (EU/APAC).

Agreed (high level) from today
- Latency targets (P95 end-to-end, client-to-response):
  - US: <= 200 ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens)
  - EU: <= 250 ms
  - APAC (Singapore region): <= 350 ms
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming supported (SSE/ws). Target per-token latency <= 60 ms from model emit to client stream for US region; slightly higher targets in EU/APAC due to egress and inter-region hops.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline support for 200 concurrent requests with sustained throughput ~500 req/min; ability to handle bursts to 1,000 concurrent short requests for short windows (minutes).
- Data residency: EU customer PII must remain in EU region; APAC-sensitive data to stay within APAC where possible. Cross-region failover acceptable only for non-PII traffic or with explicit consent.

Action items / next steps
1) Redwood to propose a lightweight test plan (latency harness + sample payloads) and confirm what data we need from Finova to run tests (anonymized sample inputs, target traffic profile). (Owner: Marissa / Aditya) — attached: redwood-slo-summary.pdf
2) Finova to confirm whether the APAC routing requirement is strict data residency or soft preference for latency routing. Also share security contact for SOC2 and encryption questions. (Owner: John)
3) Technical sync (30-45m) with Finova infra + Redwood runtime team to align on routing policy and warm-up strategy. Proposed windows: next Tue/Wed morning PST.
4) We’ll include a recommended routing policy (regional pinning + failover rules) and a proposed SLA appendix for the pilot. (Owner: Redwood)

Notes: we expect engineering to run 3-4 test passes (US/EU/APAC) over a week once we have test creds and sample payloads. Happy to dial into your security meeting if that helps.

Attachments: redwood-slo-summary.pdf (SLO summary + suggested routing), proposed-test-plan.md (working draft will follow)

Thanks —

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Data residency: for EU customers we require that any PII (names, emails, account IDs tied to EU customers) be stored and processed within the EU. For APAC, we prefer routing to Singapore (ap-southeast-1) and would like any regulated data kept within APAC.
- Streaming: our front-end requires token-by-token streaming for the chat UI. We care about both per-token latency and consistent ordering (no token gaps).
- Concurrency: the 200 concurrent baseline sounds right for pilot. For peak days we have seen short bursts up to ~800 concurrent small requests.

Questions for Redwood:
1) How does Redwood guarantee EU-only processing for PII? Is there an option to pin model evals and KV/cache to a region?
2) How does warm-up/burst handling work for models that require an initial cold start? What are typical warm-up times for the model classes you recommended?
3) We’ll need SOC2 evidence and the standard security questionnaire. Our security team (security@finova.com) is on cc.

We’re happy to do the technical sync next Wed 10:00am PST if that works for your team.

-John

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing — post-call recap & next steps

Hi all —

Following up with the technical detail and proposed test plan. I've kept this focused so your infra team can kick off quickly.

1) Regional routing / data residency- Policy options:
   a) Region pinning (recommended for PII): Pin traffic by customer region (EU customers -> eu-central-1; APAC customers -> ap-southeast-1). KV/cache and model execution remain in-region.
   b) Nearest-region routing with PII filter: Route by geo-IP for latency-sensitive requests but block PII payloads from crossing regions (requires client to mark PII or Redwood proxy to strip).
   c) Failover rules: Primary region with secondary failover to nearest region for non-PII only.

2) Latency expectations (empirical guidance for short prompts, <=512 tokens, batch size 1, streaming enabled)
   - US (us-west/us-east): P50 ~40-70ms, P95 ~140-200ms (end-to-end), token-to-client streaming latency ~20-60ms
   - EU (eu-central): add ~40-80ms to US numbers for cross-region variance; P95 ~180-260ms
   - APAC (ap-southeast): add ~120-180ms; P95 ~280-360ms
Note: these numbers assume model variant quantized for throughput and a warmed KV cache. Cold starts can add 2-10s depending on model size and instance pool.

3) Warm-up & burst handling- Strategy:
   - Keep a small pinned pool of warm instances for critical routes (reduces cold start to ~200-400ms for new requests).
   - Proactive ramp: during expected windows, issue background prefill requests to prefill KV/cache.
   - Autoscaling: horizontal scaling plus fast-path cold-start mitigations (layered container snapshots).

4) Model variants & quality tradeoffs- Recommendation for pilot:
   - Use a quantized 8-bit variant for baseline (best throughput/cost). Validate quality on your eval set.
   - Keep a higher-precision variant (fp16) for high-quality fallbacks where latency budget allows.

5) Proposed test plan (attached as proposed-test-plan.md; summary below)
   - Test passes: run separate passes from US/EU/APAC with identical payloads. Each pass:
     * Warm-up phase: 5 minutes ramp with background prefill (10% of target load).
     * Steady-state: 10 minutes at target throughput (baseline: 500 req/min; concurrency target: 200).
     * Burst windows: 3x short bursts (1 minute) at 1,000 concurrent short requests.
     * Streaming validation: continuous token streaming for 100 sample conversations; measure per-token latency and token ordering correctness.
   - Metrics to collect: P50/P95/P99 latency, per-token streaming latency distribution, error rate, tail CPU/GPU load, KV cache hit ratios, network egress times.
   - Artifacts we need from Finova: sample anonymized payloads (or synthetic equivalent), expected sequence length distribution, expected concurrency/traffic shape, test API key (time-limited), and list of IP ranges for geo validation.

6) Timeline & next steps
   - If we get sample payloads + test key by Tue EOD, we can run initial US/EU passes by end of next week and share histograms.
   - Estimated 2 engineer-days to run full multi-region passes and produce the results + config examples.

Attachments: latency-test-results-schema.csv (schema & example columns), proposed-test-plan.md
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-finova-testplan

Please reply if this plan aligns or if you want adjustments (e.g., different burst profile or longer run durations). Happy to join the sync Wed 10:00am PST.
